entries.title: Browser games
entries.summary: Plain three.js plus Rapier is the default game stack; a fixed-timestep loop, an action-map input layer, and headless hooks that let a test step the game deterministically.

entries.title: Generative art and creative coding
entries.summary: WebGPURenderer with TSL for shader art and GPU compute; determinism from a seeded PRNG, never Math.random(), Date.now() or frame time, for platforms that hash the output.

entries.title: Maps and geospatial in 3D
entries.summary: 3D Tiles for real-world photogrammetry and terrain, globe.gl for data globes, MapLibre custom layers for maps; rebase coordinates to avoid float jitter at planet scale.

entries.summary: Show a GLB with AR in one tag, or build a custom three.js configurator with material variants, image-based lighting and tone mapping tuned for color accuracy.

entries.title: Scroll-driven storytelling and hero sections
entries.summary: One persistent canvas driven by a GSAP timeline scrubbed with ScrollTrigger and smoothed by Lenis, with a poster fallback and a reduced-motion branch.

entries.title: Gaussian splat scenes
entries.summary: Split by scene size: three r186's native WebGPU splat renderer for small to medium scenes, Spark on WebGL2 for large or streamed ones; KHR_gaussian_splatting is now ratified.

entries.title: Video output and turntables
entries.summary: Frame-exact MP4, WebM, GIF or ProRes from a three.js page, driven by a virtual clock instead of wall-clock capture, for turntables, loops and social clips.

entries.title: WebXR experiences
entries.summary: Quest Browser, Chrome on Android XR and Safari on visionOS are the real targets; iPhone Safari has no WebXR at all, so iOS "AR" means AR Quick Look, not WebXR.

entries.title: 3d-tiles-renderer
entries.summary: OGC 3D Tiles for three.js, Babylon.js and R3F, with plugins for Google Photorealistic Tiles and Cesium ion; the base of most three.js geospatial work.

entries.title: camera-controls
entries.summary: Renderer-agnostic orbit and dolly controls with fitToBox and scripted transitions; a drei dependency and a common OrbitControls upgrade for product viewers.

entries.title: cannon-es
entries.summary: Pure-JS physics engine with no release since 2022; keep it only for an existing project, and move new work to Rapier or Jolt.

entries.title: deck.gl
entries.summary: GPU-accelerated map and data layers for millions of points, built on luma.gl rather than three.js; mixing it with a three.js scene needs custom layers or a shared context.

entries.title: drei
entries.summary: Helper library for React Three Fiber; controls, loaders, Environment, Text, ScrollControls; v10 is stable on WebGL, v11 alpha is the WebGPU line.

entries.title: globe.gl
entries.summary: One-call data globes (arcs, points, hexbins) built on three-globe; the fastest path to a globe visualization without owning the scene graph.

entries.title: glTF Transform
entries.summary: Scripted and CLI glTF optimization (Meshopt, Draco, KTX2, simplification, joining); the default asset pipeline for every scenario that ships a GLB.

entries.title: gltfpack
entries.summary: One-shot CLI GLB compressor built on meshoptimizer; writes Meshopt-compressed glTF that three r186's loader reads natively.

entries.title: GSAP
entries.summary: Timeline and ScrollTrigger animation library, free for all commercial use since 2025; the default engine for scroll storytelling and scripted camera moves.

entries.title: Immersive Web SDK (IWSDK)
entries.summary: Meta's three.js-plus-ECS framework for Quest-first WebXR, with the most complete agent tooling (an MCP runtime) of any three.js-based stack; still pins an old three fork.

entries.title: Jolt Physics
entries.summary: WASM rigid-body engine for large scenes, vehicles and character virtual controllers; three ships a JoltPhysics addon that loads it from a CDN.

entries.title: Lenis
entries.summary: Smooth-scroll library that honors prefers-reduced-motion by default; pairs with GSAP's ticker for one shared rAF loop in scroll storytelling.

entries.title: lil-gui
entries.summary: Small dependency-free debug panel for vanilla three.js; the current answer to dat.gui, which three itself still bundles an older copy of.

entries.title: model-viewer
entries.summary: Google's <model-viewer> web component, built on three.js, for showing a GLB with AR (Scene Viewer on Android, Quick Look on iOS) in one tag.

entries.title: Needle Engine
entries.summary: Unity- and Blender-to-web runtime built on a three.js fork, with built-in physics, networking and XR; install the stable dist-tag, not latest.

entries.title: Plotly.js
entries.summary: Stock 3D chart types (scatter3d, surface, mesh3d, isosurface, volume, cone) with hover and export; not three.js, but the first choice before hand-rolling a 3D chart.

entries.title: postprocessing (pmndrs)
entries.summary: Merged effect passes for WebGLRenderer (bloom, AO, DoF, and more); the WebGL-only alternative to three's own EffectComposer, with no WebGPU plan.

entries.title: Rapier
entries.summary: WASM physics engine for three.js games; the 0.21.0 line adds soft bodies and changed several method signatures from 0.19 and 0.20.

entries.title: @react-three/a11y
entries.summary: Dormant since 2022 with only a docs-build commit since; no maintained 3D accessibility library was found, so build accessibility with DOM equivalents instead.

entries.title: React Three Fiber (R3F)
entries.summary: React renderer for three.js; v9.8 is the stable line for React 19.3, v10 is an alpha with WebGPU-first hooks; when to use it, how to set it up, and what trips agents.

entries.title: React Three Rapier
entries.summary: Rapier physics for React Three Fiber through <Physics> and <RigidBody>; pinned to Rapier 0.19.2 while Rapier itself is at 0.21.0, so new Rapier features need the raw package.

entries.title: Spark
entries.summary: The most capable three.js Gaussian-splat engine, with streaming LoD and a GPU virtual memory pool; WebGL2 only in official releases, versus r186's native WebGPU splat renderer.

entries.title: stats-gl
entries.summary: FPS, CPU and GPU timing overlay for WebGL and WebGPU; the current replacement for stats.js and r3f-perf.

entries.title: Theatre.js
entries.summary: Designer-facing keyframe animation editor for three.js and R3F, frozen in public since 2024 while a 1.0 develops privately; use only when the visual editor itself is the point.

entries.title: three-mesh-bvh
entries.summary: Fast raycasts, shapecasts and BVH-based capsule collision against level meshes; 0.9.15 adds a WebGPU TSL/WGSL compute path alongside the pure-JS one.

entries.title: three-stdlib
entries.summary: WebGL-era copies of three.js addons as an npm package; drei 11 drops it, and new code should import three/addons/* directly instead.

entries.title: three-vrm
entries.summary: The durable open avatar path for three.js after Ready Player Me's shutdown; VRM 0.x and 1.0 support, MToon material, and a WebGPU node-material path.

entries.title: Threlte
entries.summary: Svelte 5 renderer for three.js; v8 supports WebGPU through a createRenderer prop, ahead of the equivalent React and Vue integrations.

entries.title: TresJS
entries.summary: Vue 3 renderer for three.js, the Vue equivalent of React Three Fiber; v5 is stable on WebGL, with experimental WebGPU through a renderer factory.

entries.title: troika-three-text
entries.summary: Worker-generated SDF text for three.js, mature on WebGLRenderer; no WebGPU support yet, so drei's Text component inherits the same limit.

entries.title: Bloom (WebGL)
entries.summary: A selective bloom glow on WebGLRenderer with EffectComposer, UnrealBloomPass and a threshold that only the bright object crosses.

entries.title: Bloom (WebGPU)
entries.summary: Selective bloom on WebGPURenderer with RenderPipeline, an MRT emissive channel and the TSL bloom() display node.

entries.title: Capture stills and video from a three.js page
entries.summary: Get a PNG, a contact sheet, or a frame-exact MP4, WebM, GIF or ProRes from a page, headless and deterministic, and check the result without watching it.

entries.title: CSS2D labels
entries.summary: Attach real, accessible DOM labels to 3D points with CSS2DRenderer and CSS2DObject, for the tens-of-labels case where troika-three-text would be overkill.

entries.title: Dispose a scene
entries.summary: Walk a scene graph and dispose every geometry, material and texture, then confirm renderer.info.memory returns to baseline across repeated swaps.

entries.title: Environment lighting
entries.summary: Light PBR materials with a generated RoomEnvironment (no download) or an HDR file through PMREMGenerator, so nothing renders black.

entries.title: Export a GLB
entries.summary: Export a scene or object to a binary GLB with GLTFExporter's parseAsync, for embedding in Office, model-viewer, or a downstream optimization pipeline.

entries.title: Fit camera to object
entries.summary: Frame any camera to any object's world-space bounding box, so a loaded model of unknown size always lands nicely in view.

entries.title: Fixed timestep loop
entries.summary: Accumulate real time and step a simulation in fixed increments, interpolating the rendered transform so motion looks smooth at any frame rate.

entries.title: Instanced scatter
entries.summary: Scatter thousands of objects with one geometry, one material and one draw call using InstancedMesh, placed with a seeded PRNG so the layout is reproducible.

entries.title: Keyboard orbit and reduced motion
entries.summary: A real keyboard rotate/zoom scheme for OrbitControls (whose default arrow keys only pan) plus a prefers-reduced-motion branch that turns off auto-rotate.

entries.title: Load a glTF with decoders
entries.summary: Wire GLTFLoader with the Draco, KTX2 and Meshopt decoders a compressed GLB actually needs, checked with tw glb first.

entries.title: Optimize a glTF
entries.summary: The gltf-transform pipeline order (dedupe, weld, simplify, resize, compress textures, compress geometry) and how to confirm it worked with tw glb.

entries.title: Raycast hover and click
entries.summary: Convert pointer events to a ray, pick from a flat array of pickable meshes, and track hover-enter/leave without re-raycasting the whole scene graph.

entries.title: Render on demand
entries.summary: Stop rendering 60 times a second for a page that mostly sits still, and only redraw when controls, resize or your own code actually asks for it.

entries.title: Resize and pixel ratio
entries.summary: Keep the canvas, camera aspect and pixel ratio all in sync on resize, capped so phones do not render 9x the pixels they need to.

entries.title: Seeded randomness
entries.summary: A tiny seeded PRNG (mulberry32) to replace Math.random() wherever a scene's layout must be reproducible: tests, generative art, and screenshot diffs.

entries.title: TSL custom material
entries.summary: A node material with colorNode and emissiveNode computed from position, UV and the renderer's own clock, with no GLSL or WGSL written by hand.

entries.title: Upgrade an old project
entries.summary: Find a project's current three.js release, lint what breaks moving to r186, and fix the light-intensity and color-space changes a clean lint pass does not catch.

entries.title: WebGPU backend check
entries.summary: Detect at runtime whether WebGPURenderer actually got the WebGPU backend or fell back to WebGL 2, and force each path deliberately for testing.

entries.title: Teach current three.js; keep legacy for old projects
entries.summary: What counts as current in r186, what is the WebGL path (current, feature-light), what is legacy, and the release each old pattern changed in, for porting and for reading old code.

entries.title: The verification ladder (text before pixels)
entries.summary: Prove a three.js page works with the cheapest evidence first; lint, console and scene text, model report, then one small image, and what each rung costs in tokens.

entries.title: When a chart may be 3D
entries.summary: Build a 3D chart only for data with three real axes or real geometry, always rotatable, always paired with an exact-value view; hand decorative 3D back to 2D.
